faq.a: A solution holding more dissolved substance than it normally could at that temperature, usually made by dissolving lots in hot water and letting it cool. The extra comes out as crystals.

faq.q: Why do crystals need a seed or string?
faq.a: Particles find it much easier to join an existing surface than to start a crystal from nothing. A rough string or a seed crystal gives them that starting point.
asks: Why use a string to grow crystals?

faq.q: Why are crystals such regular shapes?
faq.a: The particles always stack in the same repeating pattern. Salt ions stack in cubes, so salt crystals are little cubes; the pattern decides the shape.

faq.q: How long does it take to grow crystals?
faq.a: Small crystals appear within a day or two, and bigger ones grow over a week or more as water evaporates. Keeping the jar still and undisturbed helps.
asks: How fast do sugar crystals grow?

faq.a: It is a similar idea. Cave water carries dissolved calcium carbonate, and as each drip loses some dissolved gas it leaves a tiny bit of mineral behind, often less than a millimetre a year.

facts: Table salt forms cube-shaped crystals because its sodium and chloride ions stack in a cubic pattern.
Large sugar crystals grown on a string or stick are known as rock candy.
